Hey Offgridders, So I just got back from My place in OR. I made progress on the roof and because I got so much positive feedback from this sub I took some pictures and even made a couple stop motion videos with a Gopro. The walls of the Earthbag house stood the winter perfectly with no settling or shifting which was really good news. I was kinda worried something would move and fall or sink down. Nothing moved at all after a winter of rain, snow, freeze/thaw cycles etc. So I ordered a bunch of 2x6 lumber @16' long and OSB for sheathing.

The first job was to set the roof pitch. If you remember my previous Offgridders post pictures I had left the vertical center post too long so I could cut it to what ever I wanted. The worry was if the pitch was too steep the outer rafters would be a hazard to tall people as the walls are only 7.5 feet tall. My tallest friend is 6'2 so that is what I set the rafter tips to. I chainsawed the log and built up the roof framing as you see in the pictures.

My dad and I did it in 2 full days once the materials arrived. We were short 1 roll of tar paper so when we were done we beat the rain but got dripped on anyway! :>) The next day I finished the tar paper and tacked all the OSB triangles all over the place to hold it on as I will not put real roofing on until this fall.

The woodstove was made "for temporary tents only" :>) but was well built and a perfect replacement for an old style box stove. Wood stoves in the US today are getting insanely expensive/stupid because of environmental regulations so finding a way to cheat out of an $800 woodstove without welding up a bunch of junk my self was a good feeling. If any of you want a simple sturdy woodstove get the HQ issue woodstove from Sportsman Guide. Its the shit. There is a catch though. There is only 7 feet of chimney with it and it is 4 inch not 6 inch. I cannot buy more. The roof of my place is 7.5 feet at the stove and I put the stove up on 6 cinder blocks so it just fit. If you needed a longer chimney I would just buy a single length of 4" black iron plumbing pipe and use that.

I will attach pictures here in the next hour or so so if you read this before that I am waiting on Imgur's slow ass to upload.

Here they are!! Enjoy. Now to work on the stop motion videos. Let me know what you guys think. -Telo http://imgur.com/a/YjGGl
